plan: My value is $20. Bidding above $20 risks paying more than the item's worth, which is unprofitable. Bidding exactly $20 risks winning with no gain if others bid lower. Bidding slightly below $20 (e.g., $19.9) can maximize profit if others bid close to $20, as I'll win and pay a lower price. Thus, I'll bid $19.9 to avoid overpaying and maximize potential profit.

Given my value of $29, I aim to bid below it to ensure a profit if I win. Bidding exactly $29 or higher risks zero or negative profit. I will bid slightly below my value to increase my chances of winning while ensuring a profit margin. A bid of $24 is strategic, allowing room for profit if other bids are below my value. This bid is not dominated, as bidding higher risks overpaying, and bidding much lower reduces my winning probability significantly.

Given my value of $45, I aim to bid slightly below my value to ensure a profit if I win. I will avoid bidding my full value to prevent a zero or negative profit. Since this is a single round, I will bid $40, which is high enough to potentially win against average bids but low enough to ensure a profit margin. There is no history to consider, so my strategy focuses on maximizing profit while minimizing risk.
